page: Amazon Web Services m8a.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro System. Powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9R45 processor operating at up to 4.5 GHz, the instance supplies 16 physical cores mapped directly to 16 dedicated vCPUs with a single thread per core. Memory capacity stands at 64.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory clocked at 6 GHz, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per execution core. The instance includes 8 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, contains no bundled local NVMe storage, and does not feature hardware acceleration GPUs.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional per-core computational capabilities, marked by top-tier single-core ratings in Geekbench (2835.0) and stress-ng (3778.48), alongside a top-tier Geekbench multi-core score of 21874.0. The architecture is enhanced by modern vector instructions including AVX-512 and AVX-VNNI, driving high single-threaded throughput in compression benchmarks such as gzip (41.42 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (18.17 GB/sec). Memory subsystems achieve strong ratings with 106.87 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth, while static web serving demonstrates strong network and throughput efficiency at 54.7 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m8a.4xlarge provides favorable performance per compute unit for CPU-bound tasks through its non-hyperthreaded, dedicated physical AMD cores. However, workloads requiring persistent high-speed local disk I/O face an architectural tradeoff, as the absence of integrated local storage necessitates network-attached block storage volumes. This configuration suits enterprise application servers, mid-tier in-memory caching, microservices backends, and continuous integration pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services m8a.4xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 16 dedicated x86_64 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9R45 processor running at 4.5 GHz with a single thread per core. Supported by the Nitro hypervisor, the platform integrates 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 6 GHz, providing a standard 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware accelerators and bundled local storage are absent, requiring workloads to rely on remote storage alongside an 8 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark assessments record top-tier single-core performance in both Geekbench and stress-ng, supported by strong memory bandwidth and fast compression throughput. The instance delivers robust compute density and consistent per-core execution, making it well matched for web serving, microservices hosting, intermediate data processing, and enterprise application deployments.
